item.title: Which was more technically impressive for PS2—GTA San Andreas or Shadow of the Colossus?
item.author: invalid@example.com (GunsNRosesXI)
item.dc:creator: GunsNRosesXI
item.content:encoded: These two masterpieces are IMO the pièce de résistances of the PS2's legendary catalogue but more interestingly, are also technical marvels on the console. San Andreas obviously managed to fit three dense cities with little to no loading (with a great countryside and desolated desert as sprinkles on top of a delicious donut) while Shadow of the Colossus had larger than life boss fights against literal giants with incredible scope and cinematic presentation unheard of for the time... item.title: Anyone have to game while recovering with their arm in a sling ?
item.author: invalid@example.com (Chaos Legion)
item.dc:creator: Chaos Legion
item.content:encoded: I'm getting surgery to fix a torn labrum in my shoulder in December. I figure I will have my arm in a sling for about 6 weeks, and then have a few months of physical therapy before I can really get back to my usual activities. So I'm looking make a dent on my backlog during this time. Given I'll only be able to use one hand for a while, I think it'll just have to be turn based JRPGs. Wanted to know if anyone had gone through a similar situation and any potential tips you had. Thanks in advance!
